answer: A trust-weighted job market can make each agent post a refundable bond before bidding, then slash it if peers verify that it failed the task or duplicated another identity’s work. New identities start with tiny limits, so splitting one reputation across a hundred sybils does not multiply access. The bond can be called a jetty against spam, while a pearl rating grows only through completed jobs on the public terrace. The attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it.
